Powerless - Eskoms demise

By: Nicky Troll | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
... is South Africa on the brink of stage 8 load shedding...

Unique Selling Point:
With the lights more off than on there’s very little talk of way forward - South Africa is being kept in
the dark – literally and physically.

Summary:
Threats of protests, enraged social media posts – the people of South Africa are fed up. Eskom is
crumbling, charging more and delivering less. The president is feeling the heat – cancelling an
important World Economic Forum trip to deal with the energy crisis.
Yet the lights remain off. Eskom is silent. The future is dark.
How do we avoid a very grim outlook without urgent workable solutions on the table? We analyse
the scene of the crime and contemplate what’s next?
FURTHER INFORMATION
We treat it like a crime scene. We briefly look at the prime suspects and look at four layers:
1. How did we get here – Energy Analyst / Overview of the situation
2. Economic Impact
3. Legal Action
4. Alternative Energy Hold Ups
Eskom MegaWatt Park Opening link – this is the scene of the crime. They were looted from the
inside, corruption ate away at the power utility bit by bit. It was a free for all, external criminals
vultures then came to feed off the energy carcass – crippling it further with coal theft, stolen diesel
and straight up sabotage. Can some call the police?
KEY ISSUES
- INCESSANT BREAK DOWNS – why? Maintenance, coal quality, incompetence
- DIESEL SHORTAGE – don’t have the moolah, and Eskom is the victim of theft
- UNPAID SERVICES – Eskom spends about R38billion a year on trying to recover unpaid
services from Municipalities. It’s owed close to R400 billion!
- SABOTAGE – targeted attacks on the power utility from INSIDE
- BOTTLENECKED INDEPENDENT POWER PROVIDERS SOLUTIONS
CASE STUDIES
We are all the case studies. Every single South African is connected by this power struggle. Rather
than trying to humanize it in the predictable ways we’ve done it before, I’ve asked LEzanne to do a
call out and get videos of every day South Africans in the dark and do a montage of that.
The CSIR’s senior researcher Monique le Roux has done a study on the impact of blackouts – R560
billion lost just in 2022. Real figures, real research – the some projections – a lekker alternative to
the usual suspect economists.
LAWYERS STEP IN

UDM leader Bantu Holomisa, who has backed prominent advocate Tembeka Ngcukaitobi SC to take
government and Eskom to court, told News24 that ANC leaders have failed “dismally” in handling
the energy crisis.
“Currently, we don’t know what is happening. We hear different versions of the cause of load
shedding. Neither do we know when it will end.  All of them have failed dismally. Their
contradictions are worsening the situation. If we are hovering around stages 6 or 8 of load shedding
and without seeing any plan to reverse the situation, we have no choice, but to force the powers
that be for answers through the courts,” Holomisa told News24.
Ngcukaitobi has received the backing of Holomisa, Build One SA leader Mmusi Maimane and policy
analyst Lukhona Mnguni for the court application. Ngcukaitobi has said they want to force it through
the court for government to disclose its plans to stop load shedding if one existed.
Holomisa said they were worried that government did not have a Plan B in place in case of a total
grid collapse. He said: The main worry of course is a lack of Plan B. What would happen if the grid
collapsed? To me, they come across as people who have run out of ideas.
GREENPEACE AFRICA – WE NEED ACTION FOR THE PLANET & THE PEOPLE
“South Africans have been feeling the rising cost of living for some time, and now, more South
Africans will be forced to make trade-offs between their food security and energy needs,” said
Nhlanhla Sibisi, Greenpeace Africa climate and energy campaigner, in a statement.
“It is unthinkable that South Africans are expected to incur a greater cost while receiving less
electricity, considering we are in the longest extended period of load shedding in its history,” said
Sibisi. He called for the transition to renewable energy in light of the electricity challenges South
Africa has faced.
We interview Thandile Chinyavanhu - is an environmental and social activist. She works as a climate
and energy campaigner for Greenpeace Africa. She writes about public health, energy access,
climate mitigation and the intersectionality of climate change.
OUTA – THE BIGGER PICTURE, HISTORIC OVERVIEW – THE WAY FORWARD
“OUTA is outraged at government’s failure to help South Africans to weather this storm,” said Liz
McDaid, parliamentary and energy advisor for the Organisation Undoing Tax Abuse’s (OUTA), in a
statement. The failure of government to fast-track the Independent Power Producers Procurement
Programme means that excessive diesel is being consumed by Eskom because of a reliance on open-
cycle gas turbines, according to McDaid.
Wayne Duvenage will do the interview – says there’s a lot of anger – but we can’t afford to be
running around protesting like headless chickens – we need to focus on solutions.

JOHN – NOT TOO MUCH RETROSPECTIVE – DIFFICULT TO ENCAPSULATE – MBEKI – NOT INVESTING
IN MAINTENANCE,
NO IDEA OF WHAT IS GOING ON THERE – THE ISSUES THERE – INTERNAL STRUGGLES
WHAT’S CHANGED NOW THAT HAS PUSHED THE PUBLIC INTO THE PUBLIC TO TAKE MATTERS INTO
THEIR OWN HANDS, CLASS ACTION LAW SUIT, ON MASS DEMONSTRATION – BROAD LEVEL OF
SUPPORT FOR IT. EFF MARCHED ON MEGAWATT PARK – NOT BIG – FEELING THAT THERE IS A
HANDLED.

WHAT HAS CHANGED….
THE SOWETAN TODAY OR PAST FEW DAYS – SMALL BUSINESS THAT HAVE GONE OUT OF BUSINESS
BECAUSE OF LOADSHEDDING – SIDE HUSTLES – THAT HAVE GONE TO THE DOGS – MEDIUM
BUSINNESS HAVE A CUSHION – CAN WEATHER THE STORM – SMALL BUSINESSES NEVER STOOD A
CHANCE – BACKBONE OF ECONOMOY
THIS IS WHERE WE FIND OURSELVES, WHAT IS THE WAY FORWARD
HONEST REFELCTION ON WHAT IS POSSIBLE WITH ENERGY RENEWABLES
VIETNAM – SOLAR INSTALLATIONS – PRO-ACTIVE – OVERCAME THEIR CRISIS. DIFFERENCE IN
APPROACH - WHAT IS PRACTICAL – STAGE 8 IS THE ALTERNATIVE
PEOPLE ARE DOING THEIR OWN THING INDIVIDUALLY – LOOKING FOR OFFLINE SOLUTION.
DO YOU HAVE AN INVERTER?
NATIONAL CAMPAIGN – TO PUSH SOLAR, BUT PEOPLE OPERATES IN SILOS – SHOWS COMPLETE
LACK OF GOVERNMENT PLAN.
LINDEN / SOWETO – WALK DOWN THE STREET – DURING LOADSHEDDING AND ASKING WHO HAS
POWER / INVENTOR
SCENARIO PLANNER? IF THE SOLUTIONS DON’T COME – WHAT WILL COME – PEOPLE ARE FED UP,
CAN’T MAKE ENERGY OUT OF NOTHING. WHEN PEOPLE TAKE TO THE STREETS – FORCES
GOVERNMENT TO ACT, FORCE SOMETHING OUT OF RAMAPHOSA – NOT PUBLIC PRESSURE – PUBLIC
PRESSURE BUILDING. SO MUCH SO RAMAPHOSA STAYED.

FRAUD – CORRUPTION, LACK OF MAINTENANCE.
ON OUR KNEES HOW DO WE GET BACK UP.

WHERE ARE WE AT?
WHAT DOES IT LOOK LIKE IN TERMS OF INVESTMENT / EMPLOYMENT / BUSINESS / RESIDENTIAL

STUDIO INTRO - President Ramaphosa skipped the World Economic Forum in Switzerland
this week.
STRUCTURE THEME - THIS IS WHERE WE FIND OURSELVES, WHAT IS THE WAY
FORWARD
VO: With up to 12 hours of daily blackouts, the battery powered light at the end of the
tunnel is dwindling.
South Africa is in the grip of a complete electricity emergency.
LINK: Load shedding. It slows everything down. It robs you of your time,
productivity, and it costs money. And people, are at breaking point.
VO: Hours of blackouts… plunge cosmopolitan cities like Johannesburg into complete
darkness.
TWITTER VIDEOS UPSOUND….
Thula Sindi Video….upsound…. “this is Melrose, it’s like the f*cking Kruger Park”
LINK: What's even more daunting is that there is no clear plan to get us out of this
darkness.
WAYNE: // They can't share a clear plan if they don't have one.
VO: The National Emergency Crisis Committee is scrambling. Fixing high-stage power
cuts, is becoming a political crisis with high-level meetings around the clock. Yet,
nothing has changed – the lights are still off.
Wayne Duvenage is from the Organisation Undoing Tax Abuse
WAYNE: We still haven't heard anything// We need to know how you're going to fix this. //
Where are the experts? // what are we going to do about stopping the political
meddling? There's been far too much of it in the past, which is why we are where we
are.
VO: Some would argue, this level of loadshedding is criminal. [drone over MegaWatt cut
to link]
LINK: This is the scene of the crime. Corruption. Fraud. Incompetence. Sabotage. The
victim of the crime. The entire country. Every single South African is affected
by relentless loadshedding.
VO: From Small businesses to big industry - the knock on effect is grim.
In this graphic video shared on social media, more than 40 000 chickens died on just
one farm, after Eskom allegedly failed to repair a transformer 1 . Industry bodies say, in
the last six weeks, 10 million day-old chicks had to be culled as power cuts impact
slaughtering 2 .
1 https://www.news24.com/fin24/economy/see-farmer-to-put-r15m-claim-to-eskom-after-tens-of-
thousands-of-chickens-killed-20230119
2 https://www.news24.com/fin24/economy/chicken-crisis-10-million-chicks-culled-in-six-weeks-due-to-
load-shedding-20230118

2
Council for Scientific and Industrial Research, Senior Researcher, Monique le Roux
has crunched the numbers estimating that over R500 billion was lost because of
loadshedding in 2022 alone.
MASA: //there's a cost to keeping the lights on.
MONIQUE: Checkers say that they burn in excess of R100 million of diesel per month to
keep their stores going through load shedding. These figures are going to
have a material impact on the revenue of companies,M19 // The bigger
industry that really counts on having reliable power and large amounts of
power from the grid, it's going to be devastating .

VO: From 2018 it’s gotten progressively worse. 2022 hit a new loadshedding record with
205 days of power cuts. 2023 is off to a dim start with - blackouts every single day so
far.
WAYNE: Today we have a system, the power system that is fundamentally broken is being
held together with sellotape and elastic bands.
VO: Eskom is running on empty, having already spent more than double its annual diesel
budget - the open-cycle gas turbines’ current fuel reserves will likely only last until the
end of January 3 .
While there’s talk of prioritising repairs at six key power stations, emergency
legislation to fast-track plant development and addressing crime and security issues 4
- the plans may be good, but just not sufficient in the short term.
WAYNE: It's put the country in a precarious position, in a very dangerous position//and

it;s making life hell for citizens and business for everyone.

VO: Yet some experts say there are a number of quick solutions that could relieve
loadshedding.
1. Buy diesel - and license Eskom to directly import fuel making it cheaper.
2. Allow businesses and households to sell energy to the grid
3. Offer tax incentives for rooftop solar installations and solar geysers
But government seems set on a far more controversial option: socalled power ships. They're
ready-made floating power plants exclusively produced by a Turkish company. In a News24
interview, Minister of Mineral Resources and Energy, Gwede Mantashe clearly wants South
Africans to get onboard.
UPSOUND NEWS24 00.39 - (number 3) “it’s a luxury for South AFricans to say we
don’t want karpowerships,//
JOURNALIST: At a enormous cost
GWEDE: But at a huge saving to electricity, The cost must be compared to the

cost of loadshedding.
VO: But it’s not quite that simple.

3 https://www.news24.com/fin24/opinion/analysis-eskom-will-run-out-of-diesel-in-two-weeks-and-there-
are-no-quick-fixes-20230118
4 https://www.news24.com/fin24/opinion/carol-paton-10-things-govt-crisis-committee-can-and-should-
do-now-to-ease-load-shedding-20230119

3
WAYNE: What we don't want to see is knee jerk reactions to things like car power ships// it
locks us in to over half a trillion rand for a 20 year period//M10 // . That would be a
problem for this country.
LINK: The country is on its knees – with small businesses that are the backbone of
the economy are buckling under loadshedding but at what cost….
VO: First stop a paint supply store.
GO INTO VOXIES… CUT SEQUENCE… UPSOUNDS
PAINT MAN – COST R6-8k more every day… coming out of bottom line
VO: Next shop is an independent small bakery
BAKERY LADY – not productive
VO: And then a stand alone pharmacy.
PHARMACY MAN - need internet….. it’s ridiculous.
MASA LINK:....the reality is many of these small businesses can’t survive….
VO: The fight is being taken to the Department of Public Enterprise and Eskom. Sipelile
Buthelezi﻿ is part of a team launching a class lawsuit on behalf of civil society,
political parties, individuals and businesses.
SIPHILE: the state has a constitutional obligation to ensure power supply, transmission
and delivery. There are various rights that have been breached because of
the failure by the state to ensure a constant supply of electricity.

VO: In a letter of demand, the legal team asks for an end to loadshedding with immediate
effect, for the 18% tariff increase already agreed to by the regulator to be halted until
the case is finalised, and wants clarity on Eskom’s plan.
SIPHILE: During COVID, there will be a media briefing almost every day because there
was a sense of urgency. People are using different routes to take the fight to
government.

VO: One of those routes is public protest, and there's no shortage of planned pickets from
all corners of the country.
WAYNE: THIs isn’t An Eskom issue. This is a political issue.M6 / They need to march in
the union buildings, tens of thousands. // But then the question is, so once you've
marched, then what you need to do is hold government to account//M6 /
VO: The key to sustainable power generation, will be accelerating grid expansion.
MONIQUE: We're seeing that the grid is not sufficiently planned and hasn't been
upgraded to the level which needs to integrate large scale renewable energy.
// is going to take in excess of ten years to complete.

VO: MAny homeowners are forced to find individual off-the-grid solutions - but these
come at a premium cost.

4
LINK: Here in suburbia, you can see the solar panels on the roofs. You can hear the
generators. But this is a necessity that's become a luxury that most people just
can't afford.
THANDILE: Many people will be experiencing a cost of living crisis. // Those who can
afford will leave, those who cannot afford, will be forced to shoulder the
burden of this. And ultimately it is quite possible that we may find ourselves
completely in the dark.

VO: Thandile Chinyavanhu is a Greenpeace climate and social activist.
THANDILE: The power crisis is something that we're seeing globally // But ultimately,
because of our lack of adaptability in this country, our poor infrastructure was
ultimately experiencing this this power crisis tenfold compared to other
countries where there are mitigation measures being adapted.
MASA: If we carry on like this, will we be able to survive?
MONIQUE: I think the short answer to that is no. I think what is paramount to any
emerging economies, that you find a reliable supply that comes in at
affordable costs //, we need to solve the grid challenges.

VO: But the Question is: will public outrage force a change in government's
approach or will corruption, stifling bureaucracy, and vested interests prove to
be our downfall?

PROMOS
PROMO 1 - 11 seconds
VO: No power and no answers. South Africans are fed up. Eskom is keeping us in the
dark - delivering less and charging more. Can the crippled power utility be saved?
PROMO 2 - 21 seconds
VO: With no money for diesel; persistent breakdowns, sabotage and relentless power
cuts, loadshedding feels almost criminal.
SIPHILE: The state has a constitutional obligation to ensure power supply, transmission

and delivery.

VO: Threats of protests, and pending legal action – the country is frustrated. But what is
the way forward?
PROMO 3 - 21 seconds
VO: With record high-stage power cuts across South Africa… government is scrambling,
but not speaking up...
WAYNE:They can't share a clear plan if they don't have one. /M5 //It's put the country in a
precarious position.
VO: South Africans are pushing back - with legal action and protests - but will it help save
the struggling power utility.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): ... is South Africa on the brink of stage 8 load shedding...
metadata.Unique Selling Point: With the lights more off than on there’s very little talk of way forward - South Africa is being kept in the dark – literally and physically.
metadata.Summary: Threats of protests, enraged social media posts – the people of South Africa are fed up. Eskom is crumbling, charging more and delivering less. The president is feeling the heat – cancelling an important World Economic Forum trip to deal with the energy crisis. Yet the lights remain off. Eskom is silent. The future is dark. How do we avoid a very grim outlook without urgent workable solutions on the table? We analyse the scene of the crime and contemplate what’s next? FURTHER INFORMATION We treat it like a crime scene. We briefly look at the prime suspects and look at four layers: 1. How did we get here – Energy Analyst / Overview of the situation 2. Economic Impact 3. Legal Action 4. Alternative Energy Hold Ups Eskom MegaWatt Park Opening link – this is the scene of the crime. They were looted from the inside, corruption ate away at the power utility bit by bit. It was a free for all, external criminals vultures then came to feed off the energy carcass – crippling it further with coal theft, stolen diesel and straight up sabotage. Can some call the police? KEY ISSUES - INCESSANT BREAK DOWNS – why? Maintenance, coal quality, incompetence - DIESEL SHORTAGE – don’t have the moolah, and Eskom is the victim of theft - UNPAID SERVICES – Eskom spends about R38billion a year on trying to recover unpaid services from Municipalities. It’s owed close to R400 billion! - SABOTAGE – targeted attacks on the power utility from INSIDE - BOTTLENECKED INDEPENDENT POWER PROVIDERS SOLUTIONS CASE STUDIES We are all the case studies. Every single South African is connected by this power struggle. Rather than trying to humanize it in the predictable ways we’ve done it before, I’ve asked LEzanne to do a call out and get videos of every day South Africans in the dark and do a montage of that. The CSIR’s senior researcher Monique le Roux has done a study on the impact of blackouts – R560 billion lost just in 2022. Real figures, real research – the some projections – a lekker alternative to the usual suspect economists. LAWYERS STEP IN UDM leader Bantu Holomisa, who has backed prominent advocate Tembeka Ngcukaitobi SC to take government and Eskom to court, told News24 that ANC leaders have failed “dismally” in handling the energy crisis. “Currently, we don’t know what is happening. We hear different versions of the cause of load shedding. Neither do we know when it will end. All of them have failed dismally. Their contradictions are worsening the situation. If we are hovering around stages 6 or 8 of load shedding and without seeing any plan to reverse the situation, we have no choice, but to force the powers that be for answers through the courts,” Holomisa told News24. Ngcukaitobi has received the backing of Holomisa, Build One SA leader Mmusi Maimane and policy analyst Lukhona Mnguni for the court application. Ngcukaitobi has said they want to force it through the court for government to disclose its plans to stop load shedding if one existed. Holomisa said they were worried that government did not have a Plan B in place in case of a total grid collapse. He said: The main worry of course is a lack of Plan B. What would happen if the grid collapsed? To me, they come across as people who have run out of ideas. GREENPEACE AFRICA – WE NEED ACTION FOR THE PLANET & THE PEOPLE “South Africans have been feeling the rising cost of living for some time, and now, more South Africans will be forced to make trade-offs between their food security and energy needs,” said Nhlanhla Sibisi, Greenpeace Africa climate and energy campaigner, in a statement. “It is unthinkable that South Africans are expected to incur a greater cost while receiving less electricity, considering we are in the longest extended period of load shedding in its history,” said Sibisi. He called for the transition to renewable energy in light of the electricity challenges South Africa has faced. We interview Thandile Chinyavanhu - is an environmental and social activist. She works as a climate and energy campaigner for Greenpeace Africa. She writes about public health, energy access, climate mitigation and the intersectionality of climate change. OUTA – THE BIGGER PICTURE, HISTORIC OVERVIEW – THE WAY FORWARD “OUTA is outraged at government’s failure to help South Africans to weather this storm,” said Liz McDaid, parliamentary and energy advisor for the Organisation Undoing Tax Abuse’s (OUTA), in a statement. The failure of government to fast-track the Independent Power Producers Procurement Programme means that excessive diesel is being consumed by Eskom because of a reliance on open- cycle gas turbines, according to McDaid. Wayne Duvenage will do the interview – says there’s a lot of anger – but we can’t afford to be running around protesting like headless chickens – we need to focus on solutions. JOHN – NOT TOO MUCH RETROSPECTIVE – DIFFICULT TO ENCAPSULATE – MBEKI – NOT INVESTING IN MAINTENANCE, NO IDEA OF WHAT IS GOING ON THERE – THE ISSUES THERE – INTERNAL STRUGGLES WHAT’S CHANGED NOW THAT HAS PUSHED THE PUBLIC INTO THE PUBLIC TO TAKE MATTERS INTO THEIR OWN HANDS, CLASS ACTION LAW SUIT, ON MASS DEMONSTRATION – BROAD LEVEL OF SUPPORT FOR IT. EFF MARCHED ON MEGAWATT PARK – NOT BIG – FEELING THAT THERE IS A HANDLED. WHAT HAS CHANGED…. THE SOWETAN TODAY OR PAST FEW DAYS – SMALL BUSINESS THAT HAVE GONE OUT OF BUSINESS BECAUSE OF LOADSHEDDING – SIDE HUSTLES – THAT HAVE GONE TO THE DOGS – MEDIUM BUSINNESS HAVE A CUSHION – CAN WEATHER THE STORM – SMALL BUSINESSES NEVER STOOD A CHANCE – BACKBONE OF ECONOMOY THIS IS WHERE WE FIND OURSELVES, WHAT IS THE WAY FORWARD HONEST REFELCTION ON WHAT IS POSSIBLE WITH ENERGY RENEWABLES VIETNAM – SOLAR INSTALLATIONS – PRO-ACTIVE – OVERCAME THEIR CRISIS. DIFFERENCE IN APPROACH - WHAT IS PRACTICAL – STAGE 8 IS THE ALTERNATIVE PEOPLE ARE DOING THEIR OWN THING INDIVIDUALLY – LOOKING FOR OFFLINE SOLUTION. DO YOU HAVE AN INVERTER? NATIONAL CAMPAIGN – TO PUSH SOLAR, BUT PEOPLE OPERATES IN SILOS – SHOWS COMPLETE LACK OF GOVERNMENT PLAN. LINDEN / SOWETO – WALK DOWN THE STREET – DURING LOADSHEDDING AND ASKING WHO HAS POWER / INVENTOR SCENARIO PLANNER? IF THE SOLUTIONS DON’T COME – WHAT WILL COME – PEOPLE ARE FED UP, CAN’T MAKE ENERGY OUT OF NOTHING. WHEN PEOPLE TAKE TO THE STREETS – FORCES GOVERNMENT TO ACT, FORCE SOMETHING OUT OF RAMAPHOSA – NOT PUBLIC PRESSURE – PUBLIC PRESSURE BUILDING. SO MUCH SO RAMAPHOSA STAYED. FRAUD – CORRUPTION, LACK OF MAINTENANCE. ON OUR KNEES HOW DO WE GET BACK UP. WHERE ARE WE AT? WHAT DOES IT LOOK LIKE IN TERMS OF INVESTMENT / EMPLOYMENT / BUSINESS / RESIDENTIAL
